newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates ends up, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates ends up, seen stable.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed firmer on Friday after central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said he hoped the overnight interbank rate would rise to five percent, but dealers saw limited room for further gains.

The interbank rate ended at 4.999 percent against Thursday's 4.982 close, with 30-day commercial paper at 5.00-5.10 against 5.00. Liquidity remained loose and dealers said the interbank rate was likely to move around the five percent level.
The government bond market was quiet in the afternoon and traders expected a consolidation phase to continue.
